```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r load-packages}
library(tidyverse)

options(bdat602.source_only = TRUE)
source("courses/bdat-602/_teacher/resources/datasets/simulate_bdat602_data.R")
health_data <- simulate_bdat602(n = 500000, seed = 602)
```

## Task 1: Detect outliers using the IQR rule and Z-score

### claim_amount

```{r task1-iqr-claim}
q1_claim  <- quantile(health_data$claim_amount, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
q3_claim  <- quantile(health_data$claim_amount, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
iqr_claim <- q3_claim - q1_claim
hi_claim  <- q3_claim + 1.5 * iqr_claim
lo_claim  <- q1_claim - 1.5 * iqr_claim

n_outliers_claim <- sum(
  health_data$claim_amount > hi_claim | health_data$claim_amount < lo_claim,
  na.rm = TRUE
)
cat("Q1:", q1_claim, " Q3:", q3_claim, " IQR:", iqr_claim, "\n")
cat("Upper fence:", hi_claim, " Lower fence:", lo_claim, "\n")
cat("Outliers in claim_amount (IQR rule):", n_outliers_claim, "\n")
```

```{r task1-zscore-claim}
mu_claim <- mean(health_data$claim_amount, na.rm = TRUE)
sd_claim <- sd(health_data$claim_amount, na.rm = TRUE)
z_claim  <- (health_data$claim_amount - mu_claim) / sd_claim
n_z_claim <- sum(abs(z_claim) > 3, na.rm = TRUE)
cat("Z-score outliers (|z| > 3) in claim_amount:", n_z_claim, "\n")
# Z-score finds more outliers than the IQR rule because the skewed distribution
# inflates the standard deviation, pulling the threshold inward.
```

### bmi

```{r task1-iqr-bmi}
q1_bmi  <- quantile(health_data$bmi, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
q3_bmi  <- quantile(health_data$bmi, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
iqr_bmi <- q3_bmi - q1_bmi
hi_bmi  <- q3_bmi + 1.5 * iqr_bmi
lo_bmi  <- q1_bmi - 1.5 * iqr_bmi

n_outliers_bmi <- sum(
  health_data$bmi > hi_bmi | health_data$bmi < lo_bmi,
  na.rm = TRUE
)
cat("Upper fence for bmi:", hi_bmi, "\n")
cat("Outliers in bmi:", n_outliers_bmi, "(includes injected values like 120, 150, 200)\n")
```

## Task 2: Box plots

```{r task2-boxplot-claim}
health_data |>
  filter(claim_amount > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = claim_amount)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "steelblue", outlier.alpha = 0.1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar) +
  labs(title = "Claim Amount — Box Plot (non-zero claims)", y = "Claim Amount (USD)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r task2-boxplot-bmi}
health_data |>
  ggplot(aes(y = bmi)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "darkorange", outlier.colour = "red", outlier.alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "BMI — Box Plot (injected outliers visible in red)", y = "BMI") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Task 3: Winsorise claim_amount

```{r task3-winsorise}
p1_claim  <- quantile(health_data$claim_amount, 0.01, na.rm = TRUE)
p99_claim <- quantile(health_data$claim_amount, 0.99, na.rm = TRUE)

health_data <- health_data |>
  mutate(claim_amount_win = pmin(pmax(claim_amount, p1_claim), p99_claim))

cat("p1  (1st percentile):", p1_claim, "\n")
cat("p99 (99th percentile):", p99_claim, "\n")
cat("Original max:", max(health_data$claim_amount, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Winsorised max:", max(health_data$claim_amount_win, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
# The winsorised max equals p99 — all values above p99 are now capped.
```

## Task 4: Log transformation and before/after comparison

```{r task4-log}
health_data <- health_data |>
  mutate(
    log_claim = log(claim_amount + 1),
    log_bmi   = log(bmi)
  )
```

```{r task4-histograms}
p_raw <- health_data |>
  filter(claim_amount > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = claim_amount)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "steelblue") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::dollar) +
  labs(title = "Raw claim_amount", x = "Claim Amount") +
  theme_minimal()

p_log <- health_data |>
  filter(claim_amount > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = log_claim)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "darkorange") +
  labs(title = "log(claim_amount + 1)", x = "log(Claim Amount + 1)") +
  theme_minimal()

library(patchwork)
p_raw + p_log

# Shape before: strongly right-skewed, with a very long tail to the right.
# Shape after: approximately bell-shaped (slightly left-skewed), with far fewer
# extreme values. The log transform makes the distribution much more suitable
# for regression modelling.
```
